title: Racism killed son, mom says; Woman testifies at inquest into fatal shooting, saying police treated troubled son 'like an animal': [ONT Edition]
article: The mother of a psychologically troubled young black man whowas shot four times and killed by police officers in 2004 told an inquest yesterday her son would probably still be alive if he were white.

On the first day of the coroner's inquest into the death of O'Brien Christopher-Reid, lawyer Peter Rosenthal, representing Jacqueline Christopher, and lawyer Gary Clewley, representing the three police officers who shot the 26-year-old, carried out a legal joust in front of inquest coroner Dr. James Edwards.
In late 2004, the officers were cleared of any wrongdoing in the shooting by the province's Special Investigations Unit.
But that didn't stop Rosenthal from inviting Christopher to tell the inquest what she was most upset about. Her scathing 15-minute account of the confrontation left the room dead silent.
"They treated him like an animal," she said, unable to contain her emotions after almost two hours of earlier questioning.

"They got a call that he was walking with a knife - no complaints, no threats - they approached him and said 'Get down'. You don't tell him why you're telling him to get down, you don't explain anything to him
Christopher's voice grew louder as she continued, detailing what she described as systemic racism within the Toronto Police department.
"Because you're in a uniform, if that's how you're trained the taxpayer's money isn't doing what it's supposed to do."

When Rosenthal later invited the deceased's father to answer a question about his attitude toward police, Clewley stood up in objection and said, "We've already had one speech today and in my respectful opinion that's one too many. Mr. Rosenthal is trying to turn this into some type of soap box or discourse on race relations."
Dr. Edwards refused to let the father answer the question, stating that it had nothing to do with the circumstances surrounding Christopher-Reid's death.
On June 13, 2004, the victim was confronted by police officers at Edwards Gardens, near Lawrence Ave. and Leslie St., where he had been seen carrying a knife.

Three officers approached Christopher-Reid near a bridge as he held an extension cord. According to the SIU report, they used pepper spray, which had no effect on him. He broke free from the officers, who pursued him until he suddenly stopped and pulled a knife from his pants. He then moved toward the officers, the report states.
The officers raised their guns and ordered Christopher-Reid to drop the knife.
He refused, continued to approach them, and all three fired at close range, less than 10 feet.
Christopher began her testimony yesterday by outlining the psychiatric problems her son was dealing with shortly before his death.

She testified that she had gone to a justice of the peace in 2003 to give police permission to take her son to Scarborough Grace hospital for a psychiatric evaluation. After a six-day stay in November 2003, her son signed himself out of the hospital.
The psychiatrist who evaluated Christopher-Reid is expected to testify today.
The inquest continues throughout the week.
